findings.message: CAF Surcharge is not an allowed charge type under the contract.

Line 7: 36 * 56.00 = 2016.00. However, the contract rate for 40GP detention is 56.00 per container day with 10 free days. The invoice calculates 36 days * 56.00 = 2016.00, but the charge should only apply to days beyond free time (36 - 10 = 26 days). 26 * 56.00 = 1456.00. Overcharge = 2016.00 - 1456.00 = 560.00.
Detention charged for 36 days, but contract allows 10 free days for 40GP. Charge should be for 26 days (36-10) at 56.00/day = 1456.00. Billed 2016.00.

The billed rate for Sea Freight Charges (OFR) is 95954.17 INR per container (191908.33 / 2), which exceeds the contract rate of 2184.50 USD (2184.50 * 87.85 = 191,439.33 INR) for 40GP in the first half of 2026. Wait, let me re-calculate. The invoice says 40' Dry Standard. Contract rates for 40GP (first half 2026) is 2184.50 USD. 2184.50 * 87.85 = 191,439.33 INR. The billed rate is 191,908.33 / 2 = 95,954.17 INR. This is much lower. Let me re-read the invoice. The line total is 383,816.66 for 2 units. 383,816.66 / 2 = 191,908.33 per unit. The contract rate for 40GP is 2184.50 USD. 2184.50 * 87.85 = 191,439.33 INR. The billed rate is 191,908.33 INR. Overcharge = 191,908.33 - 191,439.33 = 469.00 INR per container. Total overcharge = 469.00 * 2 = 938.00 INR.

The billed rate for Bunker Adjustment Factor (BAF) is 44,231.60 / 2 = 22,115.80 INR per container. The contract rate for FUEL_SURCHARGE (BAF) for 40GP is 503.49 USD. 503.49 * 87.85 = 44,231.60 INR. Wait, 44,231.60 / 2 = 22,115.80. The contract rate is 503.49 USD * 87.85 = 44,231.60 INR. The billed rate is 22,115.80 INR. This is actually lower. Let me re-check the math. 44,231.60 / 2 = 22,115.80. Contract rate is 44,231.60. So it's not an overcharge. Let me re-examine line 1.
Total excl. Tax (571,771.06) + IGST @ 5% (28,588.55) = 600,359.61. This is correct.
The B/L Fee (DOC) is billed twice on this invoice.
The charge 'Main Carriage' is billed twice for the same service.
The charge 'Terminal Hdlg Chg (Origin)' is billed twice, once on line 3 and again on line 4.
The billed detention rate of 32.50 is higher than the contract rate of 26.00 per container day. For 5 chargeable days (19 total days - 14 free days), the expected amount is 130.00 instead of 162.50.
The billed rate of 3,189.05 per container is higher than the contract rate of 2,922.12 for 40HC containers on the INMAA to BEANR lane.
The billed rate of 269.00 per container is higher than the contract rate of 234.00 for 40HC containers on the INMAA to BEANR lane.

The billed demurrage is incorrect. For 2 containers, with 10 days from arrival (Jun 12) to release (Jun 22) and 4 free days, the billable amount should be 12 days at the contract rate of 65.00 (780.00), not 20 days at 81.00 (1,620.00).
The invoice applied a 5% tax rate (USD 314.03), but the contract specifies a 0% tax rate for USD invoices.
The billed rate for Export Terminal Fee (151.84) is higher than the contract rate for THC_ORIGIN (130.00).
Facility Security Charge is billed twice (Line 6 and Line 7).
Detention was billed for 19 days, but the contract allows 10 free days. Only 9 days should be charged (9 * 33.00 = 297.00). Overcharge is 627.00 - 297.00 = 330.00.
The billed rate for Bunker adj. (508.19) exceeds the contract rate for FUEL_SURCHARGE (501.80) applicable for the period 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31.
Line amount 5,662.99 does not equal quantity 2 x rate 2,746.00 (5,492.00)
The unit rate of 2574.00 USD (226,105.69 INR / 87.85) is higher than the contract rate of 2573.77 USD.
Billed 34 container-days of detention, but only 6 container-days are billable (17 total days from 21-May to 07-Jun minus 14 free days, multiplied by 2 containers).
Export THC is billed twice (line 3 and line 4).

The total amount due (1,040,927.55) does not equal the sum of subtotal (991,359.57) and tax (49,567.98), which is 1,040,927.55. Wait, 991359.57 + 49567.98 = 1040927.55. The calculation is correct. Let me re-check the lines.
CAF Surcharge is not an allowed charge according to the contract.
The tax rate for USD is 0% per the contract, but 18% was charged.
The charge 'Terminal Hdlg Chg (Origin)' is billed twice.
The detention charge is for 13 days, but the contract allows 7 free days. Only 6 days (13 - 7) should be charged. Overcharge: 7 days * 46.00 = 322.00.
The billed rate of 266,152.06 INR per unit is higher than the contract rate of 3,120.92 USD (equivalent to 266,051.18 INR) for 40GP containers on this lane.
The billed rate of 6,803.64 INR is higher than the contract rate of 75.00 USD (equivalent to 6,396.00 INR).
The invoice billed 38 days of detention, but the contract allows for 14 free days, meaning only 24 days should have been charged. The overcharge is 14 days * 49.00 USD/day = 686.00 USD.
The charge 'Congestion Recovery' is not an allowed charge type under the contract.

Demurrage quantity is 10, but based on discharge date (2026-02-10) and delivery date (2026-02-15), there are 5 days total. With 4 free days, only 1 day per container should be charged. For 2 containers, the quantity should be 2.
The demurrage charge (Quay Rent) should only be for 4 days (8 total days from Feb 28 to Mar 08 minus 4 free days), but 8 days were billed.
Unit rate 158.00 USD (13,319.40 INR / 84.30) exceeds contract rate of 157.00 USD.
Unit rate 275.00 USD (23,182.50 INR / 84.30) exceeds contract rate of 234.00 USD.

The invoice billed 14 days of equipment use, but the contract allows 7 free days of detention. Based on the pickup (Dec 19, 2026) and drop-off (Jan 02, 2027), the total duration is 14 days. Subtracting the 7 free days leaves 7 billable days. The invoice billed for 14 days (14 * 46.00 = 644.00) instead of 7 days (7 * 46.00 = 322.00), resulting in an overcharge of 322.00.
The charge 'Container Seal Charge' is billed twice.
Invoice Total (9,451.42) does not equal Net Amount (9,334.84) plus Tax (0.00).
